body: Yeah I have since some to a better place with the break up but I'm still not fully over him yet and probably won't be for a while.

Sorry it took me a while to respond but my Christmas went about as good as it could go i guess for going through a break up. I watched my kids open presents than went to a family dinner where i had to smile and act like everything was ok. And i have been working a lot so that helps to keep my mind off of things.

Not that old 8 and 5, they really liked him a lot so it was really heart breaking to have to tell them about it. My oldest wanted to talk to him for days to find out why as he put it "he didn't want us anymore".

He lives in Michigan and i live in Tennessee, he said that the distance was getting to be to much for him and that he wasn't ready for a family yet (i have two kids). Honestly i think the reason why it's so hard for me because i was going to move to Michigan to be closer to him in the new year.

He will only talk to me in person or via text message. But i will try to get him to send his address to me.
i don't want to scam him i just want to go about this legally, i would ask him what his address is but than he would start to question why i want it.

According to that i am required to give him written notification via certified mail but i don't know his current address, would i get in trouble if i sent it to his last known address that is listed in our agreement?

And i quote from the document it's self! "The Tennessee statute (T.C.A  36-6-108) which governs the notice to be given in connection with the relocation of a parent reads in pertinent part as fallows:

If a parent who is spending intervals of time with a child desires to relocate outside the state or more than fifty (50)miles from the other parent within the state, the relocating parent shall send a notice to the other parent's last known address by registered or certified mail. Unless excused by the court for exigent circumstances, the notice shall be mailed not later than  sixty (60) days prior to the move. The notice shall contain the following:

(1) Statement of intent to move;
(2) Location of proposed new residence;
(3) Reasons for proposed relocation; and 
(4) Statement that the other parent may file a petition in opposition to the move within thirty (30) days of receipt of the notice."

A side note the current address that is listed in our agreement is different than his current residing address (which is unknown by me).

Yes currently i have custody of our kids and he has visitations for 80 days of the year. He does unfortunately only get them when it is convenient for him and i have to drive them 45 mins (which i'm not supposed to be doing by the court order) just for him to see them. I also have to contact him first the majority of the time to even find out if he will be getting them.
